evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.text: The database says oracle-bone forms sometimes include 步 with 戉 as phonetic, and that the graph was first borrowed from 戉 for 歲 and later differentiated by adding dots to the 戈-shaped element; some forms instead use 步. It reports oracle-bone use for ‘year’, citing Xu Zhongshu’s proposal that one harvest season counted as a year. Later bronze forms include year/years, and later bronze variants add 月 or bamboo-slip forms add 日. These are the database’s account; it does not establish a single uncontested original graph analysis.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — oraclePiece

evidence.source: 說文解字在線查詢 / 說文解字注
evidence.text: The Shuowen entry defines 歲 as Jupiter, says it traverses the twenty-eight lunar mansions and completes a circuit in twelve months, and analyzes the graph as 从步戌聲. Duan Yucai glosses 步 as regular celestial motion and also treats 戌 as carrying phonetic and associative force. This is an early lexicographic analysis, not direct confirmation of the graph’s original formation.
evidence.title: 說文解字「歲」— Shuowen.org

evidence.text: This page reports a different account: oracle-bone forms may represent a ritual name, and it gives examples interpreted as ritual use and as ‘year’ (including 來歲); it also records disagreement over whether early form elements depict an implement, blood/dots, or 步. It cites a specific oracle-bone example ‘辛卯卜王貞、來歲、邑受年。四月’ and explains the calendrical link between Jupiter and year as an interpretation. The page’s exact source references should be consulted before treating its supplied dated corpus examples as independently verified.
evidence.kind: secondary paleographic dictionary with cited primary examples
evidence.title: 歲 — 漢字私註

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫（Chinese University of Hong Kong）
evidence.text: The database reports earliest oracle-bone forms with 戉-like shapes, later differentiated graphs, forms with 步, and subsequent bronze and Warring States variants. It describes the later small-seal graph as 从步戌聲, matching Shuowen, and notes 戉, 歲, 月 in the same Old Chinese rhyme group while 戌 belongs to a nearby group. Its account supports a proposed phonetic role for 戉 in an early form and 戌 in the transmitted seal form, but does not provide independently reconstructed readings of 戉 and 戌 on this page.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — oraclePiece

evidence.field: Middle Chinese and Old Chinese readings; definition examples
evidence.text: The page gives 歲 Middle Chinese Baxter sjwejH, fanqie 相銳切, and Old Chinese Baxter–Sagart *s-qʷʰat-s; it separately lists Zhengzhang *sqʰʷads and *sqʰʷad as variant rhyme-group readings. It lists modern Mandarin suì and Cantonese seoi3. The local Baxter–Sagart table row supplied in this research packet agrees with the page’s 歲 row (MC sjwejH; OC *s-qʷʰat-s); local rows are not independent external evidence. Its component 戉 reconstruction is not independently verified here, so no phonetic sound match between 戉 and 歲 is asserted beyond the cited paleographic analysis.
evidence.title: 歲 — Wiktionary

evidence.text: The page says simplified 岁 was adapted from the cursive form of traditional 歲, and calls 山 and 夕 shorthand shapes for 步 and 戉 respectively. It labels its displayed oracle-bone, early Western Zhou bronze, Shuowen seal, and Eastern Han clerical forms with approximate periods. The simplified form’s shape history is reported here; its modern visible subshapes should not be read as independent semantic components.

gaps: The original referent and pronunciation of the earliest 戉-like or dotted graph are not independently established here; therefore the claimed sound relationship between a named weapon/tool and the borrowed word cannot be fully tested.

CUHK’s accessible account and the other opened reference describe competing models: early graph borrowing/differentiation and ritual-use interpretations versus a movement/phonetic analysis. Primary inscription images and full corpus contexts were not inspected, so the earliest sense and precise dated attestations remain provisional.

The semantic development among ritual use, year/harvest, age, and Jupiter is not demonstrated as a continuous chronology. The Jupiter-to-year calendrical explanation is reported by lexicographic sources, but should not be treated as proof of the earliest spoken sense.

The Shuowen seal-form analysis is 步 + 戌; early-form 戉 and transmitted-form 戌 are distinct claims. No verified pronunciation/reconstruction pair for 戉 and 歲 in one reconstruction system was obtained, so no explicit sound comparison is supplied.

Official Unicode Unihan character pages for 岁, 歲, 步, 戉, and 戌 were inaccessible through the browser. The supplied local kMandarin rows confirm 岁 and 歲 as suì, but cannot substitute for external click-through evidence; component readings were not locally supplied.
